/-!
# Bloch and Landau constants

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloch%27s_theorem_(complex_analysis))
- [CP96] Chen, H., Gauthier, P. M. "On Bloch's constant." Journal d'Analyse Mathématique 69 (1996),
  275–291.
- [AG37] Ahlfors, L. V., Grunsky, H. "Über die Blochsche Konstante." Mathematische Zeitschrift 42
  (1937), 671–673.
- [Ya95] Yanagihara, H. "On the locally univalent Bloch constant." Journal d'Analyse Mathématique
  65 (1995), 1–17.
- [Ra43] Rademacher, H. "On the Bloch-Landau Constant."" American Journal of Mathematics 65 (1943),
  387–390.
- [OptimizationConstants](https://teorth.github.io/optimizationproblems/constants/57c.html)
- [Skin2009] Skinner, Brian. The univalent Bloch constant problem. Complex Variables and Elliptic
  Equations 54 (2009), no. 10, 951–955.
- [MathWorld](https://mathworld.wolfram.com/BlochConstant.html)
- [Bhowmik–Sen](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/canadian-mathematical-bulletin/article/improved-bloch-and-landau-constants-for-meromorphic-functions/FD465D1F2CEF7E8C62AFF16C3E89B7B4)
-/
open scoped Topology ENNReal
open Metric Set Filter
namespace Bloch

/-- The **Bloch radius** $B_f$ of a function $f$ is the supremum of radii of univalent disks in the
image of the unit disk under $f$. Takes values in `ℝ≥0∞` so that functions whose image contains
arbitrarily large univalent disks correctly get radius `⊤` rather than `0`. -/
noncomputable def blochRadius (f : ℂ → ℂ) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  sSup (ENNReal.ofReal '' {r : ℝ | ∃ S ⊆ ball (0 : ℂ) 1, ∃ x, ball x r ⊆ f '' S ∧ InjOn f S})

@[category API, AMS 30]
lemma zero_le_blochRadius (f : ℂ → ℂ) : 0 ≤ blochRadius f := zero_le

@[category API, AMS 54]
lemma dis_add_radius_le_of_ball_subset_ball {X 𝕜 : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup X]
    [NormedSpace 𝕜 X] [Nontrivial X] {x y : X} {r d : ℝ} (hpos : 0 < r) (hsub : ball x r ⊆ ball y d) :
    dist x y + r ≤ d := by
  have : Tendsto (fun s => dist x y + s) (𝓝[<] r) (𝓝 (dist x y + r)) :=
      (tendsto_nhds_of_tendsto_nhdsWithin tendsto_id).const_add _
  refine le_of_tendsto this ?_
  filter_upwards [Ioo_mem_nhdsLT hpos] with t ⟨hl, hr⟩
  by_cases! hxy : x = y
  · obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := exists_ne (0 : X)
    simp_all only [dist_self, zero_add]
    let u := (‖v‖⁻¹ : 𝕜) • v
    have : ‖u‖ = 1 := by apply norm_smul_inv_norm; grind
    calc
    _ = ‖y + (t : 𝕜) • u - y‖ := by simp_all [norm_smul, abs_of_nonneg hl.le]
    _ ≤ d := by
      refine (mem_ball_iff_norm.1 (hsub (mem_ball_iff_norm.2 ?_))).le
      simp_all [norm_smul, abs_of_nonneg hl.le]
  · let u := (‖x - y‖⁻¹ : 𝕜) • (x - y)
    have : ‖u‖ = 1 := by apply norm_smul_inv_norm; grind
    calc
    _ = ‖x - y‖ + t := by
      simp [NormedAddCommGroup.dist_eq]
      rw [← norm_neg (-x  + y)]
      simp [add_comm, sub_eq_add_neg]
    _ = ‖x + (t : 𝕜) • u - y‖ := by
      simp [u, add_sub_right_comm, ← smul_assoc]
      nth_rw 2 [← one_smul 𝕜 (x - y)]
      rw [← add_smul, norm_smul]
      norm_cast
      rw [abs_of_nonneg (by positivity), add_mul, one_mul, mul_assoc, inv_mul_cancel₀ (by aesop),
        mul_one]
    _ ≤ d := by
      refine (mem_ball_iff_norm.1 (hsub (mem_ball_iff_norm.2 ?_))).le
      simp_all [norm_smul, abs_of_nonneg hl.le]

@[category API, AMS 54]
lemma radius_le_of_ball_subset_ball {X 𝕜 : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup X]
    [NormedSpace 𝕜 X] [Nontrivial X] {x y : X} {r d : ℝ} (hpos : 0 < r)
    (hsub : ball x r ⊆ ball y d) : r ≤ d :=
  trans (by simp) (dis_add_radius_le_of_ball_subset_ball (𝕜 := 𝕜) hpos hsub)

@[category API, AMS 30]
lemma blochRadius_id_eq_one : blochRadius id = 1 := by
  apply le_antisymm
  · -- blochRadius id ≤ 1: every valid radius r satisfies r ≤ 1
    apply sSup_le
    rintro _ ⟨r, ⟨S, hS, x, hball, -⟩, rfl⟩
    simp only [image_id] at hball
    by_cases hpos : 0 < r
    · exact (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal
        (radius_le_of_ball_subset_ball (𝕜 := ℂ) hpos (hball.trans hS))).trans
        (by simp [ENNReal.ofReal_one])
    · exact (ENNReal.ofReal_of_nonpos (by linarith)).le.trans zero_le
  · -- 1 ≤ blochRadius id: ball 0 1 ⊆ id '' ball 0 1
    rw [show (1 : ℝ≥0∞) = ENNReal.ofReal 1 from by simp]
    exact le_sSup ⟨1, ⟨ball (0 : ℂ) 1, Subset.rfl, 0, by simp⟩, rfl⟩

/-- The **Landau radius** $L_f$ of a function $f$ is the supremum of radii of disks contained in
the image of the unit disk under $f$. Takes values in `ℝ≥0∞` so that functions with unbounded
image correctly get radius `⊤`. -/
noncomputable def landauRadius (f : ℂ → ℂ) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  sSup (ENNReal.ofReal '' {r : ℝ | ∃ x, ball x r ⊆ f '' (ball (0 : ℂ) 1)})

/-- The **Bloch constant** $B$ is the largest radius such that every holomorphic function on the
unit disk with $f'(0) = 1$ has a schlicht (univalent) disk of that radius in its image. -/
noncomputable def blochConstant : ℝ :=
  sSup {B : ℝ | ∀ f : ℂ → ℂ, DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball 0 1) → deriv f 0 = 1 →
    ∃ S ⊆ ball 0 1, ∃ x, ball x B ⊆ f '' S ∧ InjOn f S}

/-- It is proved in [CP96] that the Bloch constant is bounded below by
$\sqrt{3}/4 + 2 \times 10^{-4}$ -/
@[category research solved, AMS 30]
theorem blochConstant_lower_bound : Real.sqrt 3 / 4 + 2 * 10 ^ (-4 : ℤ) ≤ blochConstant := by
  sorry

/-- It is proved in [AG37] that the Bloch constant is bounded above by
$\frac{1}{\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{3}}}\frac{\Gamma(1/3) \Gamma(11/12)}{\Gamma(1/4)}$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 30]
theorem blochConstant_upper_bound :
    blochConstant ≤ Real.Gamma (1 / 3) * Real.Gamma (11 / 12) /
    (Real.Gamma (1 / 4) * Real.sqrt (1 + Real.sqrt 3)) := by
  sorry

/-- Ahlfors and Grunsky also conjectured in [AG37] that this upper bound is the precise value of the
Bloch constant. -/
@[category research open, AMS 30]
theorem blochConstant_exact_value :
    blochConstant = Real.Gamma (1 / 3) * Real.Gamma (11 / 12) /
    (Real.Gamma (1 / 4) * Real.sqrt (1 + Real.sqrt 3)) := by
  sorry

/-- The **Univalent Bloch constant** $B_u$ is the largest radius such that every univalent
holomorphic function on the unit disk with $f'(0) = 1$ has a schlicht disk of that radius in its
image. -/
noncomputable def univalentBlochConstant : ℝ :=
  sSup {B : ℝ | ∀ f : ℂ → ℂ, InjOn f (ball 0 1) → DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball 0 1) →
    deriv f 0 = 1 → ∃ S ⊆ ball 0 1, ∃ x, ball x B ⊆ f '' S ∧ InjOn f S}

/-- It is proved in [Skin2009] that the Univalent Bloch constant is bounded below by $0.5708858$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 30]
theorem univalentBlochConstant_lower_bound : 0.5708858 ≤ univalentBlochConstant := by
  sorry

/-- The Univalent Bloch constant is trivially bounded above by the Bloch radius of the identity
function, which is $1$. This is the best upper bound we know according to [OptimizationConstants]. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 30]
theorem univalentBlochConstant_upper_bound : univalentBlochConstant ≤ 1 := by
  apply csSup_le
  · -- the set is nonempty: 0 is in it (ball x 0 = ∅ ⊆ anything)
    exact ⟨0, fun f _ _ _ => ⟨∅, empty_subset _, 0, by simp⟩⟩
  · -- every B in the set is ≤ 1
    intro B hB
    have h := hB id (injOn_id _) differentiableOn_id (by simp)
    rcases h with ⟨S, hS, x, hball, -⟩
    simp only [image_id] at hball
    by_cases hpos : (0 : ℝ) < B
    · exact radius_le_of_ball_subset_ball (𝕜 := ℂ) hpos (hball.trans hS)
    · linarith

/-- The **Landau constant** $L$ is the largest radius such that every holomorphic function on the
unit disk with $f'(0) = 1$ has a disk of that radius contained in its image. -/
noncomputable def landauConstant : ℝ :=
  sSup {B : ℝ | ∀ f : ℂ → ℂ, DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball 0 1) → deriv f 0 = 1 →
    ∃ x, ball x B ⊆ f '' (ball 0 1)}

/-- It is proved in [Ya95] that the Landau constant is bounded below by $0.5 + 10 ^ {-335}$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 30]
theorem landauConstant_lower_bound : 0.5 + 10 ^ (-335 : ℤ) ≤ landauConstant := by
  sorry

/-- It is proved in [Ra43] that the Landau constant is bounded above by
$\frac{1}{\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{3}}}\frac{\Gamma(1/3) \Gamma(5/6)}{\Gamma(1/6)}$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 30]
theorem landauConstant_upper_bound :
    landauConstant ≤ Real.Gamma (1 / 3) * Real.Gamma (5 / 6) / Real.Gamma (1 / 6) := by
  sorry

/-- In [Ra43], Rademacher says that he strongly believed that this upper bound is the precise value
of the Landau constant. -/
@[category research open, AMS 30]
theorem landauConstant_exact_value :
    landauConstant = Real.Gamma (1 / 3) * Real.Gamma (5 / 6) / Real.Gamma (1 / 6) := by
  sorry

end Bloch

findings.description: The set S in lines 45–46 is arbitrary; `InjOn f S` does not make it an analytic inverse sheet. By choosing one preimage of each image point, the defining condition is equivalent to ordinary disk containment in `f '' ball 0 1`. I proved, without sorry, `∀ f, blochRadius f = landauRadius f`. A concrete separation was also proved in Lean: the current radius of `fun z : ℂ => z ^ 2` is 1, whereas every disk covered injectively from an open subset of the unit disk by this function has radius at most 1/2.
findings.source_evidence: Bhowmik–Sen, Introduction, p. 1269 (https://doi.org/10.4153/S0008439523000346): a univalent disk Δ means that there exists a domain Ω in D such that f maps Ω univalently onto Δ. MathWorld (https://mathworld.wolfram.com/BlochConstant.html) likewise requires a 'subregion S', not an arbitrary set of representatives.
findings.suggested_fix: Require openness of the inverse sheet: use `∃ S ⊆ ball (0 : ℂ) 1, IsOpen S ∧ ∃ x, ball x r ⊆ f '' S ∧ InjOn f S`. For holomorphic f this suffices: restricting S further to the preimage of the target disk gives the required univalent domain. Alternatively, explicitly require a holomorphic inverse branch.

findings.description: Lines 118–119 repeat the arbitrary-subset defect independently of `blochRadius`. Consequently this definition is exactly `landauConstant`, rather than the Bloch constant. The equality was proved in `/workspace/review/scratch.lean` using only ordinary Mathlib lemmas and classical choice. This is not an equivalent characterization: the cited literature distinguishes B ≤ 0.471862… from L > 1/2.
findings.source_evidence: Bhowmik–Sen, pp. 1269–1270 (https://doi.org/10.4153/S0008439523000346), defines B using univalent disks covered from domains, defines L using mere image containment, and gives the disjoint bounds B ≤ 0.4719… and L > 1/2 + 10^(-335). Wikipedia's 'Bloch’s and Landau’s constants' section also distinguishes these constants: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloch%27s_theorem_(complex_analysis).
findings.suggested_fix: Add `IsOpen S` to this definition as well as to `blochRadius`, preferably through a shared predicate for a genuine univalent disk. Retain the existing normalization and supremum over universally guaranteed radii.

findings.description: Because the current `blochConstant` equals `landauConstant`, this declaration states the numerical lower bound for L, not Chen–Gauthier's lower bound for B. The numerical expression itself is correct; this is a consequence of the defective definition, not a separate coefficient error.
findings.source_evidence: Wikipedia's constants section and Bhowmik–Sen, pp. 1269–1270, attribute the lower bound sqrt(3)/4 + 2·10^(-4) to Chen–Gauthier specifically for the Bloch constant B: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloch%27s_theorem_(complex_analysis), https://doi.org/10.4153/S0008439523000346.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct `Bloch.blochConstant` by requiring an open inverse sheet. The displayed lower-bound expression need not change.

findings.description: With the current definition, this asserts L ≤ 0.4718616534…, which conflicts with the known L > 1/2. Ahlfors–Grunsky's bound concerns B instead. The gamma expression is faithful; the incorrect meaning of the left-hand side causes the defect.
findings.source_evidence: Bhowmik–Sen, pp. 1269–1270 (https://doi.org/10.4153/S0008439523000346), records B ≤ Γ(1/3)Γ(11/12)/(Γ(1/4)√(1+√3)) ≈ 0.4719, while L > 1/2 + 10^(-335). MathWorld gives the same Bloch upper-bound expression: https://mathworld.wolfram.com/BlochConstant.html.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the definition of `blochConstant`; retain the right-hand side and the solved category.

findings.description: The declaration currently identifies the Landau constant with the conjectured Bloch value, approximately 0.4718616534. That is not the Ahlfors–Grunsky conjecture and is incompatible with the known Landau lower bound. This is a statement defect inherited from `blochConstant`, not evidence that the genuine open conjecture has been settled.
findings.source_evidence: MathWorld explicitly attributes the conjecture B = Γ(1/3)Γ(11/12)/(Γ(1/4)√(1+√3)) to Ahlfors and Grunsky: https://mathworld.wolfram.com/BlochConstant.html. Bhowmik–Sen p. 1270 confirms this and separately records the different Landau conjecture and bounds: https://doi.org/10.4153/S0008439523000346.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct `blochConstant` to require an open inverse sheet. Keep this numerical conjecture and its open category.

findings.description: The docstring says that functions with unbounded image get radius `⊤`. Unboundedness of the image does not imply arbitrarily large contained disks. For example, the normalized holomorphic function f(z) = (1/2)log((1+z)/(1-z)) maps the unit disk onto the unbounded strip |Im w| < π/4, whose Landau radius is the finite number π/4. The Lean definition correctly measures contained disks; only the explanation is wrong.
findings.source_evidence: Bhowmik–Sen p. 1269 defines L_f as the radius of the largest disk in f(D), not as a test of whether f(D) is unbounded: https://doi.org/10.4153/S0008439523000346. MathWorld uses the same supremum-of-contained-disks definition: https://mathworld.wolfram.com/LandauConstant.html.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'functions with unbounded image' by 'functions whose unit-disk image contains disks of arbitrarily large radius'.

findings.description: The inequality `univalentBlochConstant ≤ 1` and its proof are correct, but the docstring overstates this as the best known upper bound. The file's Wikipedia reference already records a smaller bound for the corresponding injective-function constant A. Independently, the normalized strip map (1/2)log((1+z)/(1-z)) gives B_u ≤ π/4 < 1. The OptimizationConstants table lists the trivial bound 1, but its incomplete table does not justify claiming that no better bound is known.
findings.source_evidence: Wikipedia's 'Bloch’s and Landau’s constants' section records `0.5 < A ≤ 0.7853` for injective holomorphic functions: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloch%27s_theorem_(complex_analysis). The cited OptimizationConstants page lists 1 as a trivial upper bound: https://teorth.github.io/optimizationproblems/constants/57c.html.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the sentence claiming that 1 is the best known upper bound, or describe it only as the trivial bound listed by OptimizationConstants. The theorem can remain unchanged.

findings.description: The docstring includes an extra factor `1 / sqrt(1 + sqrt 3)` which is absent from both the Lean statement and the cited Landau bound. Including that factor would give approximately 0.328672, contradicting the known lower bound L > 1/2. The Lean formula, approximately 0.543259, is correct.
findings.source_evidence: Bhowmik–Sen p. 1270 gives Rademacher's bound L ≤ Γ(1/3)Γ(5/6)/Γ(1/6), without the Bloch prefactor: https://doi.org/10.4153/S0008439523000346. Wikipedia gives the same expression: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloch%27s_theorem_(complex_analysis).
findings.suggested_fix: Delete `\frac{1}{\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{3}}}` from the docstring; do not add it to the Lean statement.

reformulations.difference: The source defines L as the infimum of the individual radii L_f, whereas Lean takes the supremum of radii for which every normalized holomorphic function actually contains a disk.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Admissible radii for each function are downward closed. If c = inf_f L_f, every r < c is an actual admissible radius for every f: choose an admissible radius greater than r from the definition of L_f and shrink its disk. Conversely, every universally admissible radius is at most every L_f, hence at most c. Taking the supremum gives c regardless of endpoint attainment. Radius zero is always admissible, and the identity bounds the uniform radii by 1, so the real supremum has no empty-set or unbounded-set default-value problem.

reformulations.difference: Unlike the defective unrestricted Bloch definitions, this declaration can legitimately omit `IsOpen S` from its existential subset condition.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Here `InjOn f (ball 0 1)` is already a hypothesis. If a disk is contained in f(S) for some S ⊆ D, it is contained in f(D), and D itself is an open injective witness. Conversely an open witness is an arbitrary witness. This equivalence with the condition augmented by `IsOpen S` was proved in `/workspace/review/boundaries.lean`. For holomorphic injective f, restricting to the inverse image of the target disk supplies the source's univalent domain.

demonstrated.claim: The current definition equals the Landau radius for every function and assigns radius 1 to z ↦ z², whose standard Bloch radius is 1/2.
The current definitions satisfy Bloch.blochConstant = Bloch.landauConstant, identifying the intended distinct constants.

not_demonstrated.reason: Rewriting the defective definition identifies this as a Landau lower bound, but independently proving the numerical inequality requires a nontrivial analytic estimate; the imported admitted bounds were not used.

An independent disproof requires a nontrivial Landau lower bound and a rigorous estimate showing that the displayed gamma expression is below 1/2; the elementary definition equality alone does not establish the negation.
An independent disproof likewise needs the analytic separation between Landau's constant and the displayed gamma value, rather than just the elementary definition equality.

trivial_proof.lean:
import FormalConjectures.Wikipedia.Bloch

/-!
The missing openness condition collapses Bloch's notions to Landau's.
Only definitions, classical choice, and proved API lemmas are used below.
-/
open Metric Set
open scoped ENNReal

namespace BlochTrivial

-- Bloch.blochRadius / Bloch.blochConstant: choosing one preimage per point
-- makes the injective-subset condition equivalent to ordinary image containment.
private theorem disk_iff (f : ℂ → ℂ) (r : ℝ) :
    (∃ S ⊆ ball (0 : ℂ) 1, ∃ x, ball x r ⊆ f '' S ∧ InjOn f S) ↔
      ∃ x, ball x r ⊆ f '' (ball (0 : ℂ) 1) := by
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨S, hS, x, hball, _⟩
    exact ⟨x, hball.trans (image_mono hS)⟩
  · rintro ⟨x, hx⟩
    obtain ⟨S, hS, hi, heq⟩ := Set.SurjOn.exists_subset_injOn_image_eq hx
    exact ⟨S, hS, x, heq.symm.subset, hi⟩

-- Bloch.blochRadius: as defined, it equals the Landau radius for EVERY function.
theorem radii_equal (f : ℂ → ℂ) : Bloch.blochRadius f = Bloch.landauRadius f := by
  unfold Bloch.blochRadius Bloch.landauRadius
  simp only [disk_iff]

-- Bloch.blochConstant: as defined, it equals Landau's constant, although the
-- standard constants satisfy B < 1/2 < L (Bhowmik–Sen, Introduction, pp. 1269–1270).
theorem constants_equal : Bloch.blochConstant = Bloch.landauConstant := by
  unfold Bloch.blochConstant Bloch.landauConstant
  simp only [disk_iff]

-- Bloch.blochRadius: z ↦ z² gets radius 1 here, whereas its standard Bloch radius
-- is 1/2: a genuine inverse disk must avoid 0 and lie inside the unit disk.
theorem square_radius_is_one : Bloch.blochRadius (fun z : ℂ => z ^ 2) = 1 := by
  have himage : (fun z : ℂ => z ^ 2) '' ball 0 1 = ball 0 1 := by
    ext w
    constructor
    · rintro ⟨z, hz, rfl⟩
      simp only [mem_ball, dist_zero_right, norm_pow] at *
      nlinarith [norm_nonneg z]
    · intro hw
      obtain ⟨z, rfl⟩ := (Complex.isSquare w).exists_sq
      refine ⟨z, ?_, rfl⟩
      simp only [mem_ball, dist_zero_right, norm_pow] at *
      nlinarith [norm_nonneg z]
  simpa only [radii_equal, Bloch.landauRadius, himage, image_id]
    using Bloch.blochRadius_id_eq_one

#print axioms radii_equal
#print axioms constants_equal
#print axioms square_radius_is_one

end BlochTrivial

  65 (1995), 1–17.
- [Ra43] Rademacher, H. "On the Bloch-Landau Constant."" American Journal of Mathematics 65 (1943),
  387–390.
- [OptimizationConstants](https://teorth.github.io/optimizationproblems/constants/57c.html)
- [Skin2009] Skinner, Brian. The univalent Bloch constant problem. Complex Variables and Elliptic
  Equations 54 (2009), no. 10, 951–955.
- [MathWorld](https://mathworld.wolfram.com/BlochConstant.html)
- [Bhowmik–Sen](https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/canadian-mathematical-bulletin/article/improved-bloch-and-landau-constants-for-meromorphic-functions/FD465D1F2CEF7E8C62AFF16C3E89B7B4)
-/
open scoped Topology ENNReal
open Metric Set Filter
namespace Bloch

/-- The **Bloch radius** $B_f$ of a function $f$ is the supremum of radii of univalent disks in the
image of the unit disk under $f$, covered injectively from open subsets of the unit disk.
Takes values in `ℝ≥0∞` so that functions whose image contains arbitrarily large univalent disks
correctly get radius `⊤` rather than `0`. -/
noncomputable def blochRadius (f : ℂ → ℂ) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  sSup (ENNReal.ofReal '' {r : ℝ | ∃ S ⊆ ball (0 : ℂ) 1, IsOpen S ∧
    ∃ x, ball x r ⊆ f '' S ∧ InjOn f S})

@[category API, AMS 30]
lemma zero_le_blochRadius (f : ℂ → ℂ) : 0 ≤ blochRadius f := zero_le

@[category API, AMS 54]
lemma dis_add_radius_le_of_ball_subset_ball {X 𝕜 : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup X]
    [NormedSpace 𝕜 X] [Nontrivial X] {x y : X} {r d : ℝ} (hpos : 0 < r) (hsub : ball x r ⊆ ball y d) :
    dist x y + r ≤ d := by
  have : Tendsto (fun s => dist x y + s) (𝓝[<] r) (𝓝 (dist x y + r)) :=
      (tendsto_nhds_of_tendsto_nhdsWithin tendsto_id).const_add _
  refine le_of_tendsto this ?_
  filter_upwards [Ioo_mem_nhdsLT hpos] with t ⟨hl, hr⟩
  by_cases! hxy : x = y
  · obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := exists_ne (0 : X)
    simp_all only [dist_self, zero_add]
    let u := (‖v‖⁻¹ : 𝕜) • v
    have : ‖u‖ = 1 := by apply norm_smul_inv_norm; grind
    calc
    _ = ‖y + (t : 𝕜) • u - y‖ := by simp_all [norm_smul, abs_of_nonneg hl.le]
    _ ≤ d := by
      refine (mem_ball_iff_norm.1 (hsub (mem_ball_iff_norm.2 ?_))).le
      simp_all [norm_smul, abs_of_nonneg hl.le]
  · let u := (‖x - y‖⁻¹ : 𝕜) • (x - y)
    have : ‖u‖ = 1 := by apply norm_smul_inv_norm; grind
    calc
    _ = ‖x - y‖ + t := by
      simp [NormedAddCommGroup.dist_eq]
      rw [← norm_neg (-x  + y)]
      simp [add_comm, sub_eq_add_neg]
    _ = ‖x + (t : 𝕜) • u - y‖ := by
      simp [u, add_sub_right_comm, ← smul_assoc]
      nth_rw 2 [← one_smul 𝕜 (x - y)]
      rw [← add_smul, norm_smul]
      norm_cast
      rw [abs_of_nonneg (by positivity), add_mul, one_mul, mul_assoc, inv_mul_cancel₀ (by aesop),
        mul_one]
    _ ≤ d := by
      refine (mem_ball_iff_norm.1 (hsub (mem_ball_iff_norm.2 ?_))).le
      simp_all [norm_smul, abs_of_nonneg hl.le]

@[category API, AMS 54]
lemma radius_le_of_ball_subset_ball {X 𝕜 : Type*} [RCLike 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup X]
    [NormedSpace 𝕜 X] [Nontrivial X] {x y : X} {r d : ℝ} (hpos : 0 < r)
    (hsub : ball x r ⊆ ball y d) : r ≤ d :=
  trans (by simp) (dis_add_radius_le_of_ball_subset_ball (𝕜 := 𝕜) hpos hsub)

@[category API, AMS 30]
lemma blochRadius_id_eq_one : blochRadius id = 1 := by
  apply le_antisymm
  · -- blochRadius id ≤ 1: every valid radius r satisfies r ≤ 1
    apply sSup_le
    rintro _ ⟨r, ⟨S, hS, -, x, hball, -⟩, rfl⟩
    simp only [image_id] at hball
    by_cases hpos : 0 < r
    · exact (ENNReal.ofReal_le_ofReal
        (radius_le_of_ball_subset_ball (𝕜 := ℂ) hpos (hball.trans hS))).trans
        (by simp [ENNReal.ofReal_one])
    · exact (ENNReal.ofReal_of_nonpos (by linarith)).le.trans zero_le
  · -- 1 ≤ blochRadius id: ball 0 1 ⊆ id '' ball 0 1
    rw [show (1 : ℝ≥0∞) = ENNReal.ofReal 1 from by simp]
    exact le_sSup ⟨1, ⟨ball (0 : ℂ) 1, Subset.rfl, isOpen_ball, 0, by simp⟩, rfl⟩

/-- The **Landau radius** $L_f$ of a function $f$ is the supremum of radii of disks contained in
the image of the unit disk under $f$. Takes values in `ℝ≥0∞` so that functions whose unit-disk
image contains disks of arbitrarily large radius correctly get radius `⊤`. -/
noncomputable def landauRadius (f : ℂ → ℂ) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  sSup (ENNReal.ofReal '' {r : ℝ | ∃ x, ball x r ⊆ f '' (ball (0 : ℂ) 1)})

/-- The **Bloch constant** $B$ is the largest radius such that every holomorphic function on the
unit disk with $f'(0) = 1$ has a schlicht (univalent) disk of that radius in its image. -/
noncomputable def blochConstant : ℝ :=
  sSup {B : ℝ | ∀ f : ℂ → ℂ, DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball 0 1) → deriv f 0 = 1 →
    ∃ S ⊆ ball 0 1, IsOpen S ∧ ∃ x, ball x B ⊆ f '' S ∧ InjOn f S}

/-- It is proved in [CP96] that the Bloch constant is bounded below by
$\sqrt{3}/4 + 2 \times 10^{-4}$ -/
@[category research solved, AMS 30]
theorem blochConstant_lower_bound : Real.sqrt 3 / 4 + 2 * 10 ^ (-4 : ℤ) ≤ blochConstant := by
  sorry

/-- It is proved in [AG37] that the Bloch constant is bounded above by
$\frac{1}{\sqrt{1 + \sqrt{3}}}\frac{\Gamma(1/3) \Gamma(11/12)}{\Gamma(1/4)}$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 30]
theorem blochConstant_upper_bound :
    blochConstant ≤ Real.Gamma (1 / 3) * Real.Gamma (11 / 12) /
    (Real.Gamma (1 / 4) * Real.sqrt (1 + Real.sqrt 3)) := by
  sorry

/-- Ahlfors and Grunsky also conjectured in [AG37] that this upper bound is the precise value of the
Bloch constant. -/
@[category research open, AMS 30]
theorem blochConstant_exact_value :
    blochConstant = Real.Gamma (1 / 3) * Real.Gamma (11 / 12) /
    (Real.Gamma (1 / 4) * Real.sqrt (1 + Real.sqrt 3)) := by
  sorry

/-- The **Univalent Bloch constant** $B_u$ is the largest radius such that every univalent
holomorphic function on the unit disk with $f'(0) = 1$ has a schlicht disk of that radius in its
image. -/
noncomputable def univalentBlochConstant : ℝ :=
  sSup {B : ℝ | ∀ f : ℂ → ℂ, InjOn f (ball 0 1) → DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball 0 1) →
    deriv f 0 = 1 → ∃ S ⊆ ball 0 1, ∃ x, ball x B ⊆ f '' S ∧ InjOn f S}

/-- It is proved in [Skin2009] that the Univalent Bloch constant is bounded below by $0.5708858$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 30]
theorem univalentBlochConstant_lower_bound : 0.5708858 ≤ univalentBlochConstant := by
  sorry

/-- The Univalent Bloch constant is trivially bounded above by the Bloch radius of the identity
function, which is $1$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 30]
theorem univalentBlochConstant_upper_bound : univalentBlochConstant ≤ 1 := by
  apply csSup_le
  · -- the set is nonempty: 0 is in it (ball x 0 = ∅ ⊆ anything)
    exact ⟨0, fun f _ _ _ => ⟨∅, empty_subset _, 0, by simp⟩⟩
  · -- every B in the set is ≤ 1
    intro B hB
    have h := hB id (injOn_id _) differentiableOn_id (by simp)
    rcases h with ⟨S, hS, x, hball, -⟩
    simp only [image_id] at hball
    by_cases hpos : (0 : ℝ) < B
    · exact radius_le_of_ball_subset_ball (𝕜 := ℂ) hpos (hball.trans hS)
    · linarith

/-- The **Landau constant** $L$ is the largest radius such that every holomorphic function on the
unit disk with $f'(0) = 1$ has a disk of that radius contained in its image. -/
noncomputable def landauConstant : ℝ :=
  sSup {B : ℝ | ∀ f : ℂ → ℂ, DifferentiableOn ℂ f (ball 0 1) → deriv f 0 = 1 →
    ∃ x, ball x B ⊆ f '' (ball 0 1)}

/-- It is proved in [Ya95] that the Landau constant is bounded below by $0.5 + 10 ^ {-335}$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 30]
theorem landauConstant_lower_bound : 0.5 + 10 ^ (-335 : ℤ) ≤ landauConstant := by
  sorry

/-- It is proved in [Ra43] that the Landau constant is bounded above by
$\frac{\Gamma(1/3) \Gamma(5/6)}{\Gamma(1/6)}$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 30]
theorem landauConstant_upper_bound :
    landauConstant ≤ Real.Gamma (1 / 3) * Real.Gamma (5 / 6) / Real.Gamma (1 / 6) := by
  sorry

/-- In [Ra43], Rademacher says that he strongly believed that this upper bound is the precise value
of the Landau constant. -/
@[category research open, AMS 30]
theorem landauConstant_exact_value :
    landauConstant = Real.Gamma (1 / 3) * Real.Gamma (5 / 6) / Real.Gamma (1 / 6) := by
  sorry

end Bloch
